title: Vista: A Generalizable Driving World Model with High Fidelity and Versatile Controllability

output_modality.value: front-view video at 10 Hz and 576x1024, extended by autoregressive rollout

control_signal.value: Multi-modal ego actions: high-level command and goal point, low-level trajectory, steering angle and speed.

control_mechanism.value: Unified action interface learned in a second phase with frozen pretrained weights: LoRA plus zero-initialised projection layers in all UNet attention blocks; 15% dropout per action mode; action independence constraint.

base_model.value: Initialized from Stable Video Diffusion (UNet denoiser); condition frames injected by latent replacement; dynamics enhancement and structure preservation losses; triangular classifier-free guidance.

datasets.value: OpenDV-YouTube and nuScenes for training (1:1 in action phase); evaluation on nuScenes, unseen Waymo, and also CODA and OpenDV-val in human study.

metrics.value: FID and FVD on 5369 nuScenes samples, two-alternative human evaluation (visual quality, motion rationality), Trajectory Difference via inverse dynamics model, and uncertainty-based reward.

controllability_evidence.value: Average subset FVD on nuScenes falls from 367.2 (action-free) to 322.7 goal point, 292.2 command, 230.0 angle and speed, 207.6 trajectory; Waymo 311.8 to 268.9 command, 273.7 trajectory.

closed_loop.value: No policy-in-the-loop evaluation; autoregressive long-horizon rollouts only, with 15 s predictions shown in a guidance-scale figure.

stated_limitations.value: High compute cost; degradation in long rollouts or drastic view shifts; action control can fail for ambiguous commands and goal points; training data far from all internet driving data.

notes: Figure 8 value-to-condition pairing inferred from garbled figure text; Waymo order of 311.8, 273.7, 268.9 maps to action-free, command, trajectory by label order and may be imperfect (the 273.7 and 268.9 assignment is the uncertain part).
